cases.exposure_context_quote: The cause of the phosphine poisoning was the fumigation of stored grain in an agricultural building adjacent to the building that served as a hostel. It was found that both buildings were connected by an underground corridor or a pipe through which the released poison gas penetrated.
cases.agent: aluminum phosphide (Gastoxin tablets) releasing phosphine gas
cases.agent_quote: According to subsequent information from the representative of the Police of the Czech Republic, Gastoxin tablets containing ALP, releasing the toxic gaseous phosphine, which to some extent mimics the symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning (with a considerable ability to bind to hemoglobin), were found in an adjacent building.
cases.circumstance: accidental occupational exposure: fumigation of stored grain in an agricultural building adjacent to the hostel where the patient was temporarily housed; phosphine gas penetrated via an underground corridor/pipe; initially misdiagnosed as carbon monoxide poisoning

symptoms.finding: unconsciousness (found unconscious; regained consciousness during transport)
symptoms.quote: Two male subjects were found unconscious in one of the rooms.
During admission to the hospital, the patient was somnolent, bradypsychic, and scored on the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) at 10–12.

cases.time_to_care: immediate (emergency medical crew to nearest hospital; oxygen 15 L/min en route)

treatment.name: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV
treatment.quote: hydrocortisone 100 mg, and 1500 mL of balanced crystalloids (Plasmalyte, Baxter Czech Ltd., Prague, Czech Republic) were administered intravenously.

treatment.name: balanced crystalloids (Plasmalyte) 1500 mL IV

treatment.name: hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) 2.5 ATA, 90 min isopression, single session
treatment.quote: HBOT therapy 2.5 ATA (250 kPa) was performed, 90 min of isopression, compression, and decompression at a rate of 6–8 kPa/min was administered.

treatment.name: ondansetron 8 mg IV (for nausea)
treatment.quote: The patient became nauseous and was injected intravenously with 8 mg of ondansetron.

cases.icu_admission: yes (admitted to ICU of local hospital; supportive ventilation not required)
cases.outcome: survived; discharged from hospital in a stable condition 4 days after admission with excellent final clinical outcome
cases.outcome_quote: The patient was discharged from the hospital in a stable condition 4 days after admission.
cases.sequelae: none reported; discharge in stable condition
cases.notes: One of two men found unconscious; the second man died of phosphine intoxication. Initial misdiagnosis as carbon monoxide poisoning (detector interference + COHb unit confusion). Patient without valid work permits/health insurance, from Eastern Europe. ECG: ST elevation V2-V4 (up to 2 mm in V2 on day 2); echocardiography EF 50%. No intubation required.
